1. The present Criminal Revision No. 1532 of 2003 (Raj Kumar And Another Vs. State of U.P. and Another) has preferred against judgment and order dated 22.5.2003 passed by Sri A.K. Srivastava,
Special Judge (S.C. & S.T.) Act, Varanasi dismissing the Appeal No. 193 of 1999 (Raj Kumar and another Vs. State of U.P. and another) arising out of the judgment and order dated 15.10.1999 Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129720712/
1 passed by Sri K.P. Tripathi, Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Varanasi in Criminal Case No. 6036 of 1994, State Vs. Raj Kumar and another, whereby the revisionists are convicted under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced them to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for a period of six months and to pay a fine of Rs. 1000/- each.
2. Revisionist No.2 Dashrath has expired during the course of this revision and the revision has been abated by the Court vide order dated 15.11.2019 against revisionist No.2.
3.

sentences.text: It is also submitted that Criminal Revision No.1532 of 2003 was decided by the coordinate bench of this Court vide order dated 11.11.2022 which was not on merit, therefore, he moved a Criminal Appeal No.1531 of 2023 before the Hon'ble Apex Court.

The Hon'ble Apex Court set aside the order dated 11.11.2022 and directed to set aside the impugned order dated 11.11.2022 and restored the Criminal Revision No.1532 of 2003 and directed it to decide the revision afresh after affording the opportunity of hearing to the revisionists.
4.
Brief facts of the case are that the complainant, Food Inspector inspected the shop of revisionists where flour, pulses, spices, sugar, jaggery and biscuits were placed for sale.
The complainant served notice in Form No. 6 and purchased 7.50 gms. Pulse for Rs. 8.25/kg. and divided it in three equal parts and sampled it as per provisions of law.
Accused was sought to sign it for which he denied.
The worker in the shop of accused Girdhar signed the complain as a witness.
Thereafter, they prepared sample and sent it to laboratory for analysis to CMO concerned on 16.12.1991.
As per analysis report No. 16917, 1% Dal Keshari was found adulterated with the sample which is prohibited as edible goods.

After the analysis report, complainant filed the complaint forwarded through the Medical Officer under Section 2(1)(l) of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 which is punishable under Section 7/16 of the Act.
After the written consent of Medical Officer, the complaint is filed.
5. Accused were summoned in the Court, the statement of witness, Gaya Prasad Singh was recorded under Section 244 of Cr.P.C.
The Court framed charges against accused under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and read over to the accused and the accused denied from the charges and seek trial.
6. The complainant Gaya Prasad Singh was again produced to record his evidence under Section 246 of Cr.P.C.

The prosecution produced PW-2 Ram Janam Yadav, Food Clerk in Municipal Board,
PW-3 Ashok Kumar Srivastava, Food Clerk in the office of Varanasi.

After the conclusion of prosecution witnesses, statements of accused were recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
7.

Accused stated on oath in his statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. that whole incident is wrong, no such incident happened, Food Inspector did not inspected his shop, no sample was collected by him, no papers were signed by him at the time of inspection he was not present at shop.
Accused Dashrath also stated in his statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. that he was not present at shop at the relevant point of time when the sample was collected by the Food Inspector.
8. Accused were awarded the opportunity of producing defence evidence but the accused did not produce any defence witness.

sentences.text: Hence learned trial court found on the basis of the evidence on prosecution and on the basis of Laboratory Analysis Report that the sample collected by Food Inspector was adulterated.

Learned trial court relying upon Ram Lubhaya Vs. Municipal Corporation Delhi, 1974 (4) SCC 491, State of U.P. Vs. Badri EFR 1998 (2), 2192-2020 and Halku Vs. State of U.P. EFR 1986, 100 and 101 held that, according to sections 10(7) of the Food Adulteration Act, it is mandatory to inspect the shop in the presence of independent witnesses but it is held by the Supreme Court that he need not be produced before this court for their evidence hence compliance of section 10(7) of the Food Adulteration Act has been followed properly in accordance with law.
10. On the basis of food analysis report which was proved by the witnesses, the court held that sample contains moisture of 5.8% and adulteration of Dal Khesari of 0.7%, however, the sample was not found broken or damaged by insects.

sentences.text: No chemical adulteration was found with the sample hence learned trial court found that only 1% Dal Khesari was found adulterated which is prohibited as edible goods hence convicted the accused under Section 7/16 and punished them for simple imprisonment of 6 months and fine of Rs.1000/- each.
11. Aggrieved with the judgment passed by Special Chief Judicial Magistrate-I, Varanasi, the revisionists preferred criminal revision.

12. The first revisional court, going through the record and judgment passed by the Special Chief Judicial Magistrate-I, held that the finding recorded by learned trial court is well reasoned and does not suffer any illegality or material irregularity and needs no interference and, confirmed the judgment passed by Special Judge (S.C & S.T.) Act dated 22.5.2003.
13.

Learned counsel for revisionists submits that as per analysis report, no chemical adulteration is found, the sample is not found damaged, the moisture of 5.8% was found, rest of the sample that is 99.3% was found up to the mark.
Learning trial code as well as revisional code did not consider the fact that the sample was 99.3%.
As per prescribed standard the revisionists are not previously convict nor wanted in any other case except the instant one.

The complainant Food Inspector did not obtain the signature of accused revisionists on samples or complaint, there is no independent witness to the incident hence it is prayed to set aside the judgment and order dated 15.10.1999 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-I as well as judgment and order passed by revisional court dated 22.5.2003.
14.
Learned A.G.A. submits that notice was duly served on accused, however, they refused to sign it.
The signature of their servant is taken on the complaint.
It is also stated in the complaint itself that no independent witness agreed to sign the papers.
The sample was prepared according to the provisions of law and sent for analysis.
As per analysis report proved by complainant 0.7% Khesari found adulterated in Dal Chana.

It is also submitted that as per the provisions of section 10(7), it is a mandatory requirement of law that sample should be prepared in front of one of the independent witness but it is not the requirement of law to produce them in court also.

The Peon of revisionists,
Girdhar Ram has signed the document, complainant and samples, however he could not be produced as evidence.
He is the servant of revisionists hence the judgement passed by the trial court suffers no irregularity and the revision is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: I have heard rival submissions of the parties and peruse the record.

16. The main contention of learned counsel for the revisionists is that the learned trial court as well as first revisional court analyzed the evidence of witnesses in arbitrary manner and no public witness has been produced by prosecution, the mandatory provisions are not complied with.
Section 10(7) of the Food Adulteration Act states as under:-

Where the food inspector take any action under clause (a) of Sub-section 1 and Sub-section 2, Sub-section 4, Sub-section 6, he shall call one or more persons to be present at the time when such action is taken and take his or their signature.
17. Learned counsel for the revisionists submits that the independent witness has not been produced in court during trial.
The provisions of Section 10(7) envisages the signature of independent witness or complaint on samples, however, it does not contemplate the evidence of that person during the trial too.

18. Hon'ble Apex Court held in Ram Lubhaya Vs. Municipal Corporation Delhi 1974 (4) SCC 491 that, it is mandatory to summon independent witness at the place of occurrence at the relevant time but there examination during trial is not necessary.

entities.text: Ram Lubhaya Vs. Municipal Corporation Delhi 1974 (4) SCC 491
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Section 10(7) stipulates that food inspector shall call one or more person for witnessing the proceedings of inspection, however, if they refuse for signature or cooperate with the proceedings, the Food Inspector cannot compel them for evidence.

19. In the given case, the complainant tried to summon many persons for signature on the papers as witness but they refused to participate in the proceedings, however, Peon of revisionists himself signed the papers, therefore, it cannot be termed as illegal proceedings because prosecution has undertaken the provisions of Food Adulteration Rules.
20. The second contention of learned counsel for the revisionists is that sample do not contain any material, injurious to the health of any person.
No chemical adulteration is found.
No broken or damaged or insecticide grain is found according to food analysis report and learned trial court did not take into consideration the above mentioned facts.

21. I have gone through the analysis report, wherein it is specifically mentioned that 0.7% Dal Khesari is found adulterated in Chana Dal, which is injurious to the health hence prosecution proved the factum of adulteration by cogent piece of evidence and supported it by the oral evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3.
Revisionists are also given opportunity to adduce defence, however, no defence is produced except the bare statement of denial.
22. Accused/revisionists did not disclose any prior enmity between the revisionists and the complainant, Food Inspector.
No ulterior motive to falsify the complaint is mentioned by the accused revisionists.
PW-1, Food Inspector has acted in compliance of his statutory duties imposed upon him.

4 23.

sentences.text:
There is nothing on record to suggest that the evidence of complainant is false or fabricated,
therefore, the evidence of Food Inspector cannot be brushed aside merely because he is complainant to the case and there is no independent witness.
There is no infirmity or contradiction in the statement of PW-1 to create any doubt in the statement of witnesses.
PW-1 is government official having no enmity or companionship with revisionists.
Therefore, evidence of PW-1 is uncontroverted and admissible in evidence.
24. During the course of argument learned counsel for the revisionists submitted that in case the court upheld the conviction of revisionists, the punishment may be reduced.

It is submitted that this case is 23 years old, both the revisionists are old age, they are not previously convict nor they have committed any crime after this incident, the court has not given them the benefit of First Offenders Act, he had been detained in jail for 7 days he is ready to deposit the fine whichever is decided by this Court, hence it is prayed to commute the sentence.
25.

From the above discussion, it has been proved that the complainant food inspector inspected the shop in due course of business in discharging of his official duties, he has collected the sample,
prepared the complaint which is signed by the Peon of the revisionists.

The sample was sent for analysis and as per analysis report, the sample was found adulterated with 0.7% Dal Khesari and containing moisture of 5.8%, the case is proved by prosecution beyond reasonable doubt no evidence is produced by the accused either as defence evidence or at the time of first revision that the proceedings are not in accordance with law, hence, the judgment of trial court as well as judgment passed by first revisional court suffers no irregularity, perversity, illegality and there is no ground to interfere with the impugned judgments, hence the judgement of trial court as well as first revisional court is liable to be upheld, hence the judgement with regard to the conviction of revisionists is upheld.
26.

So far as the punishment is concerned, the revisionists were taken into custody by the Court of first revision on 22.5.2003 and he was granted bail by the coordinate bench of this Court on 30.5.2003 hence he had remained in jail for 7 days and the court has awarded the fine of Rs.1000/-
each to the revisionists.
27. Looking into the fact that the case is a about 23 year old, the fine of Rs.1000/- lost his relevancy

,
the value of rupees has been depreciated hence if the amount of fine is enhanced to Rs.20,000/- it shall serve the purpose of law hence the sentence is reduced to 7 days already undergone by the revisionists and the amount of fine is enhanced to Rs.20,000/- from Rs.1000/- each.
Revisionist are directed to deposit the fine within one month from the date of judgement.
28. In the light of above discussion the revision is partly allowed.
